title: Observability and support diagnostics bundle
goal: Give enterprise operators a safe, product-level way to understand failures without reading raw shell logs or guessing which subsystem is broken.
scope: Add an observability/support diagnostics surface that summarizes app health, database migration head, worker/inline dispatch state, queue depth, active/stuck runs, tool readiness, AI provider state, feed-sync state, recent errors, and audit harness failures. Add a redacted support bundle export that includes config shape, health snapshots, recent logs, task/run IDs, and validation output without secrets or customer-sensitive evidence payloads.
generation_reason: The audit required shell inspection of `/tmp/aegispt-inline-host.log`, process state, `ss`, curl, and failed Python tracebacks to understand why the app was hanging. Enterprise users need these diagnostics in-product and exportable safely.

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement until this package is the single active task in NEXT_TASK.md.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: Diagnostics and redacted support export only. Do not expose raw secrets, full evidence payloads, credential material, or customer-sensitive task stdout by default.

success_criteria: Settings or a Diagnostics screen shows app/DB/worker/tool/feed/AI readiness in one place.
A redacted support bundle can be generated from API or UI.
Support bundle tests prove secrets, tokens, passwords, hashes, and raw evidence payloads are excluded or redacted.
Recent failures include exact subsystem, timestamp, and safe next action.
Operators can distinguish app-down, worker-down, tool-missing, feed-rate-limited, AI-disconnected, and run-stuck states.
Docs explain when to attach a support bundle and how to inspect it locally.

acceptance_criteria: A redacted diagnostics bundle is created and contains no secret material.
A failing subsystem is visible with an actionable message.

before_promotion: NEXT_TASK.md must contain this task as the only active task.
after_completion: Promote exactly one next approved task into NEXT_TASK.md.
